identity.title: When the Prompt Becomes Visual: Vision-Centric Jailbreak Attacks for Large Image Editing Models

problem.claim: The paper studies how malicious instructions can be delivered through visual inputs to large image editing models.

gap.claim: The safety risk created when the attack surface becomes visual is described as critical and underexplored.

contributions.claim: The authors propose Vision-Centric Jailbreak Attack (VJA), a visual-to-visual jailbreak attack using purely visual inputs.
The authors introduce IESBench, a safety-oriented benchmark for image editing models.
The authors propose a training-free defense based on introspective multimodal reasoning, without auxiliary guard models.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe VJA as the first visual-to-visual jailbreak attack that conveys malicious instructions purely through visual inputs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that VJA reaches attack success rates up to 80.9% on Nano Banana Pro and 70.1% on GPT-Image-1.5 on IESBench.
The authors report that their defense substantially improves the safety of poorly aligned models to a level comparable with commercial systems.
The authors report negligible computational overhead and no need for auxiliary guard models for the defense.

narrative_sequence.summary: Image editing has shifted toward inferring intent from visual inputs and visual–text prompts.
This shift makes the attack surface itself visual, creating an underexplored safety concern.
The authors introduce VJA and the IESBench benchmark to study the threat systematically.
They report high attack success on commercial models and present a low-overhead, training-free defense.

source_observation.claim: The paper pairs a newly defined attack with a dedicated safety benchmark before reporting model-specific attack rates.

lessons.interpretation: Threat claims become more concrete when the attack mechanism, evaluation resource, and reported metric are introduced together.
lessons.application: For a new attack modality, define the threat mechanism and release or specify a modality-matched benchmark before presenting comparative success rates.
lessons.exception: This may be unsuitable when a validated standard benchmark already measures the exact threat or when benchmark construction is outside the work's scope.

source_observation.claim: The proposed defense is characterized by alignment improvement, comparable safety level, absence of auxiliary guard models, and negligible overhead.

lessons.interpretation: Defense contributions can be framed through both safety outcome and deployment costs.
lessons.application: Describe a defense using its target safety change together with model dependencies and computational overhead.
lessons.exception: Avoid this framing when those deployment constraints are not measured or are irrelevant to the intended use case.

unknowns: The abstract does not define IESBench, the attack-success criterion, tested configurations, or comparison baselines.
The abstract does not report the defense's absolute safety metrics, statistical uncertainty, or generalization beyond the mentioned model categories.
The abstract does not provide enough detail to assess the authors' priority claim that VJA is first.
